summary: Singles' Day turns into a test of AI shopping assistants, and the US says it will open a dialogue with China on advanced AI at next week's APEC summit.
body: Today is Singles' Day, or Double 11, China's biggest online shopping festival. This year the story is AI. JD.com says nearly 80 million people used its AI shopping assistant during the event, more than three times last year, and on Douyin (China's TikTok) chatbot links drove about 5% of purchases in October, rising above 20% for things people research first, such as supplements, Reuters reports.[^1][^2] Tmall says sales of AI tokens, prepaid units of AI use, rose more than 700% in the run-up, and Alibaba says AI toys passed 100 million yuan (about $15 million US) in sales within a year.[^1][^2]

The bigger picture is calmer. Data firm Syntun counted festival sales up only 2.4% from Oct 7 to 31, and China's retail sales grew just 1.1% in the year to September.[^1] My read: the platforms are using AI to make shopping feel new, but households are still careful with money. Syntun publishes its full figure on Thursday.[^1]

On technology diplomacy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen at the APEC summit (Nov 18-19) to launch a dialogue on "superintelligence", including a direct line to warn each other of serious AI incidents.[^3] He also described planned mutual tariff cuts on about $30 billion of non-sensitive goods each way. China's foreign ministry calls US spying accusations involving Nvidia's chief executive "groundless".[^3]

sources.title: China's Singles' Day shopping festival puts AI selling power to the test
